tool_input.command: git stash -- app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts && bun test tests/PostController.test.ts 2>&1 | grep -E "pass|fail|Expected|Received" | head -10; git stash pop

result:
`bun test` passes (4/4) and `bun run typecheck` is clean.

The bug was in `PostController.update` (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:88`): it hand-built a `302 Found` response instead of using the framework's `this.redirect()`. A 302 preserves the request method, so after the save the browser re-issued the **PUT** against `/posts/<id>` — which is the update route itself — looping until it aborted with `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`; the write had already committed, which is why the edit appeared on reload. `store` and `destroy` were unaffected because they already go through `this.redirect()`, whose Controller implementation answers non-GET requests with `303 See Other` (and 302 for GET), forcing the follow-up to be a GET. I replaced the manual `Response` with `return this.redirect(\`/posts/${post.id}\`)` plus a short comment explaining the status choice, leaving validation handling untouched (an invalid payload still throws `ValidationException` before the redirect, yielding 422 for JSON clients and a redirect-back with errors for Inertia). I also added a `posts.update` block to `tests/PostController.test.ts` that signs in as the seeded author, creates a scratch post, asserts the save returns 303 with `Location: /posts/<id>` and that the title actually changed, and asserts a blank title is still rejected with 422; I verified the new test fails against the old 302 behaviour and cleans up its post afterwards.
